description: German Baroque master of counterpoint. His keyboard music is built from independent, equal melodic voices woven together with rigorous part-writing and a strong harmonic drive.
harmonic_language: Functional tonal harmony with driving harmonic rhythm, circle-of-fifths sequences, suspensions resolving downward, clear cadential formulas (often with a Picardy third in minor), and modulations to closely related keys.
style_notes: Write genuinely independent contrapuntal voices, each a complete melodic line; there is no mere 'accompaniment' — every voice is melodic.
Use imitation: a subject stated in one voice is answered in another (at the fifth/fourth for a fugue), then developed in episodes built from motivic fragments.
Maintain a steady, motoric rhythmic pulse (continuous sixteenth or eighth motion shared between voices).
Voice leading is strict: prepare and resolve dissonances, avoid parallel fifths and octaves, keep voices in their registers without crossing unnecessarily.
Sequences drive the harmony forward; build episodes from a one- or two-beat motivic cell transposed through a circle of fifths.
Cadences are emphatic and structural; in minor keys end on a major (Picardy) tonic.
